key_insight: EvolveNav turns zero-shot object-goal navigation from a static, one-shot process into a self-improving one by letting the agent learn from its own experience at test time. It combines proactive preflection with an evolving memory so navigation decisions get better as the agent explores.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the weakness of existing zero-shot object-goal navigation methods that depend on fixed foundation-model priors and do not adapt during deployment, causing repeated mistakes, inefficient exploration, and high trial-and-error cost.
method: Builds an agentic rule memory by extracting actionable navigation knowledge from past interactions and observations.
Uses proactive preflection to anticipate likely failures or better actions before committing to a move.
Updates memory continuously at test time, enabling the agent to self-evolve and improve navigation behavior without additional training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path to deployable embodied agents that adapt online instead of relying entirely on static pretrained knowledge. It can reduce wasted exploration and improve success rates in new environments without retraining.
visual_elements: A loop diagram showing explore → reflect → update memory → better navigation.
A before/after comparison of static-prior navigation versus self-evolving navigation.
An icon-based memory module illustrating rule extraction, storage, and reuse.
A navigation map with the agent revisiting fewer dead ends over time.
paper_title: EvolveNav: Proactive Preflection and Self-Evolving Memory for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation
paper_authors: Qi Chai, Wenhao Shen, Nanjie Yao, Yue Xia, Kaiyong Zhao
